intent: A race commentator at the finish line: breathless numbers, then the strange reason for 42.195.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Where was the FIRST marathon race run?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Where was the first marathon race run?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat
lines.text: Greece, the United Kingdom, or the USA?
Greece: at the 1896 Athens Olympics, from the town of Marathon to the stadium, about forty kilometres.

lines.direction: a person first — the real 1896 photograph rises in, an amphora pops on 'water carrier', a flash on 'won', the time card lands on 'hours'
lines.text: A Greek water carrier named Louis won it, in just under three hours.

lines.direction: the twist: two lengths rise as blocks; the UK flag-ball arrives on 'London', a castle pops on 'Windsor'
lines.text: But London 1908 stretched the course to 42.195 kilometres, so it could start at Windsor Castle.

lines.direction: let the years run, THEN vs NOW split on 'changed', an official medal pops beside NOW
lines.text: That odd distance became official in 1921, and it has not changed since. Every marathon you have ever watched ran it.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: Born in Greece, measured in London. Follow us.
